description: This figure is not a plot or micrograph but a rendered data table — "Table 1 – Microstructural and compositional characteristics of low-density Fe–Mn–Al–C steels [36]" — presented on a black title bar with the table body on a white background. Its header row is headed "Fe–Mn–Al–C steels" and defines four steel families as the four data columns: "single ferrite steel", "single austenite steel", "A-BDP steel" and "F-BDP steel". The left stub column carries two row labels: "Alloy composition (wt.%)" (spanning three sub-rows) and "Constituent phases". Under composition, each column gives printed ranges for Mn, Al and C: single ferrite steel has X_Mn < 5.0, 5.0 < X_Al < 12.0, X_C < 0.1; single austenite steel has 15.0 < X_Mn < 30.0, 2.0 < X_Al < 12.0, 0.5 < X_C < 2.0; A-BDP steel has 10.0 < X_Mn < 25.0, 5.0 < X_Al < 12.0, 0.6 < X_C < 1.0; F-BDP steel has 3.0 < X_Mn < 10.0, 3.0 < X_Al < 9.0, X_C < 0.4. The "Constituent phases" row lists the phase assemblages visible per column: δ, B2, DO3, κ for single ferrite; γ, α, δ, κ, β-Mn for single austenite; α, B2, DO3, γ, κ, β-Mn for A-BDP; and α, δ, B2, DO3, γ, κ, α′ for F-BDP. The table argues that Mn, Al and C content windows map onto distinct ferrite/austenite/duplex phase constitutions.

observations.observation: The table is titled 'Table 1 – Microstructural and compositional characteristics of low-density Fe–Mn–Al–C steels [36]', indicating the data are reproduced from reference [36].
Four steel families are defined as table columns: 'single ferrite steel', 'single austenite steel', 'A-BDP steel' and 'F-BDP steel'.
The composition row is labelled 'Alloy composition (wt.%)', so all composition values in the table are in weight percent.
single ferrite steel: X_Mn < 5.0, 5.0 < X_Al < 12.0, X_C < 0.1.
single austenite steel: 15.0 < X_Mn < 30.0, 2.0 < X_Al < 12.0, 0.5 < X_C < 2.0.
Constituent phases for single ferrite steel are listed as δ, B2, DO3, κ.
Constituent phases for single austenite steel are listed as γ, α, δ, κ, β-Mn.
Constituent phases for A-BDP steel are listed as α, B2, DO3, γ, κ, β-Mn.
Constituent phases for F-BDP steel are listed as α, δ, B2, DO3, γ, κ, α′.
The carbon range differs most sharply across columns, from X_C < 0.1 in single ferrite steel to 0.5 < X_C < 2.0 in single austenite steel.
F-BDP steel is the only column whose phase list includes the α′ phase, and A-BDP and F-BDP both list β-Mn-derived or ordered B2/DO3 phases.
The caption states the table summarises microstructural and compositional characteristics of low-density Fe–Mn–Al–C steels.
